CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: Deterministic offline/local benchmark runtime; no cloud credentials, privileged external infrastructure, internet services, or destructive host routing; preserve realistic Linux routing semantics through an isolated kernel model.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a production-style Go route control plane that models desired route and policy state, reconciles it across a multi-node Linux fleet, detects drift, protects management reachability, records revision history, and exposes the same lifecycle through an operator dashboard and Ansible-driven installation/configuration.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: policy routing rules and named tables

REQUIRED_END_STATE: At least 16 route-control API operations spanning nodes, tables, routes, rules, revisions, preview/apply/rollback, drift/reconcile, rollouts, audit, health and dashboard summary.
All route mutations target an isolated deterministic kernel model.
Desired and observed state are revisioned and restart-recoverable.
Per-node failures are isolated during wave rollout with rollback.
Ansible installs binary/config/service and projects variables idempotently.
Frontend exposes inventory, route/rule state, revisions, drift and rollouts.

STATE_MODEL.persistence: Atomic JSON checkpoint with schema version, monotonic revision, nodes, desired revisions, observed snapshots, rollouts and audit sequence; startup validates primary and last-known-good backup.
STATE_MODEL.concurrency: store-level compare-and-swap revision plus per-node apply serialization; immutable read snapshots
STATE_MODEL.safety: management CIDRs/interfaces and protected routes are explicit policy; unsafe plans are rejected before publication

outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: Seed eight deterministic nodes across three sites, fourteen named route tables, IPv4/IPv6 and multipath routes, policy rules, drift fixtures and multiple historical revisions.
